title: withdrawals/1.0 - the only channel permitted to travel forward in time
$comment: The worst failure this contract can have is a record a human has determined is NOT FAITHFUL, still being served as evidence. Both existing mechanisms -- review.yaml's faithfulness: divergent|inadequate, and the registry's superseded_by -- live inside the producer's NEXT TAG, and a consumer pins one tag and re-serves it verbatim. So with v0.1.0 pinned and v0.2.0 marking an entry inadequate, the pinned surface keeps serving the old record until a human re-pins, and nothing tells them to. Nothing in the other seven artifacts carries a `withdrawn` state. This file does, it is APPEND-ONLY, and a consumer is expected to read it from the NEWEST tag even when pinned to an older one -- the single channel allowed to move forward in time, and safe precisely because it can only REMOVE trust, never grant it.

registry_id.$comment: Which registry these withdrawals are about. A withdrawal file applied to the wrong registry would silently remove trust from keys it was never about.

withdrawals.$comment: APPEND-ONLY. An entry is never edited and never deleted: a withdrawal that could be removed is a withdrawal a consumer cannot rely on having seen. Sorted by (withdrawn_at, key) so an append is one hunk in the diff. There is deliberately NO reinstatement field -- restoring trust goes through a new registry entry and a new human review, which is the path that has a reviewer and a date on it.

reason.$comment: Free text, and mandatory. A withdrawal with no reason tells a reader that something is wrong and not what, which leaves them unable to judge whether their own use is affected.

withdrawn_by.$comment: A named human. This is a trust-removing act and it carries the same attribution discipline as the faithfulness axis -- the failure ADR-0005 names is an unattributed axis, and an anonymous withdrawal would be one.

supersedes_review.$comment: The reviewed_statement_digest this withdrawal retracts, when it retracts a specific review rather than the entry as a whole.
